title: The Inventory of the reservoir
premise: Petra Voss has spent a decade as a bridge inspector, translating his unspoken grief over his drowned brother into the precise language of expansion joints and load tolerances, while his marriage to Lena thins to a measured tolerance of its own. At his mother's funeral, a stranger addresses the family by their pre-emigration surname—a name buried with the reservoir that flooded their old neighborhood—and Petra realizes his mother kept the truth of that summer sealed inside her all along. Returning to the drowned village before the last bus route is permanently rerouted, he confronts the memory he has inspected and deferred for ten years: that he survived the ice because his brother did not. He ends by speaking the name aloud at the water's edge, then going home to say the other thing he has almost said for a decade.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is the pen name of a former municipal engineer who spent twelve years inspecting bridges across northern river valleys before turning to fiction. Their work examines how infrastructure and memory bear weight, and how both eventually require honest assessment.

chapters.title: Tolerance for Movement
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet him mid-inspection on the Kestrel Viaduct, measuring hairline fractures with the same care he uses to avoid certain conversations at home. Lena leaves a note about a counseling appointment he won't attend. The chapter establishes his creed: everything holds if you measure the give. Emotional beat: the quiet vertigo of a life engineered to never fail loudly.

chapters.title: The Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At his mother's funeral, an elderly stranger named Aldous Grieg calls the family by their original surname—Vosstran—and mentions 'the reservoir' and 'what the boy carried.' Petra's uncle silences the man. That night Petra finds his mother's inspection reports for the dam project, dated weeks before his brother's drowning. Emotional beat: the first crack in the structure he built to hold.

chapters.title: High Water Mark
chapters.summary: Alternating Petra's present journey to the drowned village with fragments of the summer of the freeze. He learns from Grieg, who once worked the dam, that the reservoir's filling was rushed, that the ice on the flooded fields was thin where the old orchard had been, and that his mother filed a complaint she withdrew. Petra stands on the shore where the church steeple breaks the surface. Emotional beat: rising dread as the story of his survival reassembles wrongly.

chapters.title: Load-Bearing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax and resolution. On the last day before the bus route closes, Petra walks the frozen shallows to the steeple and finally remembers: his brother pushed him onto the thick ice and took the thin path back. He speaks the name Vosstran, and his brother's name, aloud over the water. He rides the final bus home and, at the kitchen table, tells Lena everything—beginning with 'My name was.' Emotional beat: the weight, finally shared, holds.
